title: When Everyone Can Build a Model: Mechanistic Inference in the Age of AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.41454v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Modern deep learning and AI-assisted code generation are lowering the technical barrier to building mathematical models of biological systems that reproduce complex observations. This lets researchers with domain expertise build semi-mechanistic, hybrid models constrained by prior knowledge and augmented with learned structure without extensive training in modelling. However, easier construction does not make interpretation easier: predictive success of such so-called grey-box models does not establish that an inferred mechanism corresponds to the one that generated the data, and the learned component can absorb errors in the mechanistic part. Many biological modelling problems are underdetermined, so several, possibly infinitely many, models may reproduce the same data equally well. translated_title: 当人人都能建模时：AI时代的机制推断
translated_abstract: 现代深度学习和AI辅助代码生成正在降低构建能够重现复杂观测的生物系统数学模型的技术门槛。这使得具有领域专业知识的研究人员无需接受大量的建模训练，就能构建受先验知识约束、并通过学习到的结构加以增强的半机制性混合模型。然而，更便捷的构建并不意味着更易解释：这类所谓“灰箱”模型的预测成功并不能证明所推断的机制就是生成数据的真实机制，而且学习组件可能会吸收并掩盖机制部分中的误差。许多生物建模问题是欠定的，因此可能有多个、甚至无限多个模型能够同样好地重现相同的数据。这种模糊性体现在两个建模选择上：哪些变量可以影响其他变量，以及哪种响应函数描述了底层机制。
tldr: 该论文指出，尽管AI工具大幅降低了构建生物系统数学模型的技术门槛，使领域专家能轻松构建“灰箱”混合模型，但模型预测的成功并不能保证推断出的机制与真实机制一致——欠定性导致多个模型可能同样好地拟合数据，这为AI时代的机制推断带来了根本性的解释挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that while AI tools dramatically lower the barrier to building mathematical models of biological systems, enabling domain experts to construct grey-box hybrid models, predictive success does not guarantee that inferred mechanisms match the true data-generating mechanisms—underdetermination allows multiple models to fit the data equally well, posing fundamental interpretive challenges for mechanistic inference in the age of AI.
